## Summary — 2026-08-28 Earnings Calendar Scan

**Starting state:** Flat — no open positions, no open orders. Equity $100,000, so the 2.5–3% debit cap = $2,500–$3,000/position.

**Reviewed:** All 7 Tier-A candidates flagged by the scan (DELL, PANW, AVGO, SNOW, HPE, LULU, ZS). For each I pulled the live option chain at the scan's specified front (9/4) and back (10/2) expiries/strikes to get real OCC symbols and current bid/ask, rather than trusting the scan's mid prices or liquidity flags blindly.

**Traded (5 calendars, dry run):**

| Ticker | Front (sell) | Back (buy) | Qty | Net debit/ct | Total debit | % of equity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DELL | 470C 9/4 | 470C 10/2 | 1 | $15.65 | $1,566 | 1.57% |
| AVGO | 370C 9/4 | 370C 10/2 | 4 | $6.42 | $2,568 | 2.57% |
| SNOW | 330C 9/4 | 330C 10/2 | 4 | $7.15 | $2,860 | 2.86% |
| HPE | 55C 9/4 | 55C 10/2 | 18 | $1.60 | $2,880 | 2.88% |
| LULU | 116C 9/4 | 116C 10/2 | 12 | $2.45 | $2,940 | 2.94% |

Total capital committed: ~$12,814 (≈12.8% of equity), 5 of the 6–8 position slots used.

Sizing logic: qty = floor($3,000 cap / per-contract debit), since contracts are lumpy. DELL's per-contract debit ($1,566) is large relative to the cap, so only 1 contract fits — that lands below the 2.5% floor, which is an unavoidable rounding artifact, not a deliberate under-size.

**Skipped (liquidity):**
- **PANW** — front 9/4 382.5C quote $18.02/$22.52 (~22% of mid) and back 10/2 385C $27.80/$31.90 (~14% of mid). Despite the scan's "liquid=true" tag, the live spread is too wide to enter a clean debit; skipping.
- **ZS** — front 9/4 187.5C $11.78/$14.12 (~18% of mid) and back 10/2 187.5C $15.56/$17.99 (~14.5% of mid). Same issue — wide enough that I don't trust the fill; skipping.

No Tier B (control group) names were in this candidate list, so nothing to flag-and-ignore there.

**Not applicable today:** No existing positions, so no rolls were needed.

**Bottom line:** Opened 5 new calendar spreads (DELL, AVGO, SNOW, HPE, LULU), each sized to 2.5–2.94% of equity, well within the 6–8 position cap. PANW and ZS were passed on purely due to thin live quotes on the exact ATM contracts needed, not because the term-structure signal was weak — both still had large ratios and would be worth re-checking on a day with tighter markets.
